configs.description: EX4100-F-48T as shipped - 48 jacks without PoE, four Virtual Chassis and four uplink SFP+ cages, the built-in 90 W AC supply and one built-in front-to-back fan (Tables 16 and 26).
configs.name: ac

gaps.note: Table 17 and the callouts give the four Virtual Chassis ports as 1GbE/10GbE SFP+, while Figure 32, Table 25 and the Junos listing name them SFP+/SFP28 and give a 25 Gbps speed indication. The tables are used (10g); the cages are the same SFP-family cage either way.
gaps.wanted: Juniper's statement of the Virtual Chassis port speeds.

gaps.note: The Status lamp changes meaning with the mode button (Table 25), so the jack lamps keep the component's link and activity vocabulary and the mode lamps carry the meaning.
gaps.wanted: none beyond the component's own vocabulary.

gaps.note: The guide names the CLD lamp and sends the reader to the cloud-ready blink patterns, which it does not hold.
The claim code, serial number and CLEI labels are stickers with no content in any figure; they are named regions and are not drawn.
The earthing terminal is two bare holes for M5 screws. The library has no pair part for M5 holes on a 5/8 in pitch, so they are drawn as holes and no lug seat is offered.
gaps.wanted: a two-hole M5 earth terminal part

gaps.note: Only the 48-port CLI listing names the interfaces and the numbers are not printed on the metal, so no interfaces block is written.

gaps.wanted: A flat drawing or photograph of the lid, the underside and the side panels.

airflow.note: Table 26 and Table 16 - one built-in fan with front-to-back (AFO) cooling, cold air entering the front vents and leaving the rear. The overview says back-to-front can be ordered but the guide lists no part number or figure for it, so no back-to-front configuration is modelled.

built-in-power-and-fans.note: Tables 3, 16 and 26 and the rear callouts name a built-in 90 W AC power supply and a built-in fan, and Table 45 lists the switch "with in-built fans and power supply". The cooling overview says once that the fan modules are hot-removable field-replaceable units, but the guide has no removal or replacement procedure for a fan or a supply (its Maintain Components chapter covers transceivers and fibre only), names no part number for either, the rear callouts call them built in, and the photograph shows a round grille flush with the panel with no handle, latch or module outline. They are taken as part of the chassis, not bays and not components. The Junos listing in the guide shows a JPSU-920W-AC-AFO and fan trays for an EX4100-48P, which is a different box.

chassis.note: Tables 17 and 18 - height 1.72 in (4.37 cm), width 17.36 in (44.09 cm), depth 10.1 in (25.65 cm), weight 3885 g. The width is the body between the bracket fold lines; the guide gives no 19 in figure and the photographs show no ears. The depth 256.5 mm is the centimetre figure.

colour.note: Median of the bare front face in the photograph, #acb2bc, and of the rear, #9da4ae; the status plate reads #4c5668. The face is carried at #a3a8af, a little under the studio light, as the library does.

drawing-vs-photo.note: The guide's Figure 24 is the same studio photograph. The legends are drawn from the photograph: the model line reads EX4100-F in white with no PoE mark, and the jack and cage numbers are white. The maker's logo and Mist AI mark beside the model line are not drawn and are reserved as a logo-zone. This model's top vent field is shorter than the 48P's and its lower vent runs only under the right end.

earthing.note: Table 46 and Figure 96 - a protective earthing terminal on the rear panel for a Panduit LCD10-14A-L lug on two M5 by 10 mm screws, which are separately orderable. The photograph shows two bare holes on a lighter plate 15.7 mm apart (the 5/8 in lug pitch is 15.9) and no screws, so they are drawn as holes on the plate and no two-hole seat is offered.

lamp-size.note: The cage lamp windows are placed as common/led-arrow-sm@1 (2.25 by 2.0 mm). The photograph shows triangles about 2.8 by 2.6 mm, which common/led-arrow@1 (3.6 by 3.2) would match, but two of those overlap at the 2.95 mm step the photograph gives, so the smaller part is used.

mounting.note: Table 4 and the mounting topics - the 2-post kit SRX34X-RMK ships in the box (front-mounting brackets, two in Table 45), the four-post kit EX-4PST-RMK and the wall kit EX-WMK are orderable. The four-post kit also holds 2 in recessed front brackets, so a recess of 50.8 mm is the one measured position. No kit is listed under chassis.kits in this change, and none of the kit part numbers is modelled.

port-lamps.note: Figures 30 to 32 and Table 24 - each jack and each cage has a Link Activity lamp and a Status lamp. The jacks carry them in their keyway corners. The photograph shows four small triangular windows per cage column in the metal band between the two cage rows, two pointing down and two up; they are read as the two lamps of the upper port (the down-pointing ones, at 2.05 and 9.46 mm from the column edge) and of the lower port (the up-pointing ones, at 5.0 and 12.4), the left one of each pair being Link Activity by analogy with the jacks. No figure says which window is which, so the assignment is estimated. The Status lamp shows what the mode lamps select (Table 25), so its states cannot be one vocabulary here.

port-numbering.note: The legends under each column read 0 up-arrow, down-arrow 1, then 2 and 3 up to 46 and 47, so the upper jack of a column is the even port; all are white on this model. The cages print 0 up-arrow, down-arrow 1, 2 up-arrow, down-arrow 3 under each group, and the right group is bracketed and labelled UPLINK. The left group is the Virtual Chassis ports. The numbers are as printed, from 0. Interface names are not printed on the metal. The guide's Junos listing for a 48-port model gives ge-0/0/0 to ge-0/0/47 for the jacks, et-0/1/n, ge-0/1/n and xe-0/1/n for the four Virtual Chassis ports (PIC 1, 4x1G/10G/25G SFP/SFP+/SFP28) and ge-0/2/n and xe-0/2/n for the four uplinks (PIC 2, 4x1G/10G SFP/SFP+).

ports.note: Table 17 and Figure 26 - 48 RJ-45 ports in two rows of 24, in three shells of eight columns, then two 2x2 groups of SFP+ cages. The in-shell step is the registry's 13.97 and the shell step reads 117.5 mm, a gutter of 5.6. The rows centre 13.8 mm apart on this photograph and 14.1 on the 48P's; 14.0 is used for both. The upper row is turned 180 so that its keyway and lamps face up, as photographed. The cages are two columns by two rows, abutting on the registry's 14.25 pitch, at 360.1 and 391.8 mm; the registry's 15.0 row pitch is used for the two rows.

power.note: Tables 16, 21 and 27 - a 90 W AC supply, 100 to 240 V, 50/60 Hz; at most 70 W input. The model has no PoE. The rear legend prints 1.2A Max.

rear.note: Figures 25 and 27 and the rear photograph. From the left - the MGMT RJ-45 over a USB 2.0 Type-A port in one housing, the CON RJ-45, a lighter plate with two bare holes and the earth symbol to its right, the ESD socket and symbol below the plate, one round fan at 115.3 mm, a label field and the AC inlet at 401.9 mm with its legend above (AC INPUT 100-240V 50-60Hz 1.2A Max, printed on the metal). Five screws stand along the lower edge. This rear differs from the 48P's: the earth symbol is beside the plate and not above the console, the ESD socket is below the plate, and there is one fan. The label corner marks across the middle frame the serial number and CLEI labels (callouts 4 and 6); the claim code label (callout 8) has no corner marks in the photograph. Stickers are regions and are not drawn.

reset.note: Figure 26 callout 9 - the reset button is the small round pinhole between the legends of the two jacks of column 22, at 334.3 mm, below the jacks. It sits between two legend arrows closer than the library's 4 mm button part is wide, so it is drawn as a pinhole in the metal and not placed as a part. The Factory Reset/Mode button (callout 5) is the blue one and is a part.

scale.note: Gate 1 - both photographs are straight-on studio shots. The front face is 1405 px across and the rear 1426, against 440.9 mm that is 3.187 and 3.234 px/mm. The rear's height of 144.5 px against 43.7 mm is 3.31 px/mm, 2.2 percent above the width, so y is read at 3.307 there and x at 3.234. The jack pitch reads 44.3 px, 13.9 mm, the registry's 13.97 mm on a quantity the scale never saw. Horizontal positions are measured from the centre of the face (the left and right edges disagree by up to a millimetre in the bevel) and every position is estimated, good to about half a millimetre across and one down.

sources.note: EX4100-F Switch Hardware Guide, Juniper Networks, PDF created 2026-10-01 (271 pages; https://www.juniper.net/documentation/us/en/hardware/ex4100-f/ex4100-f.pdf): Tables 3 to 5, 16, 17, 18, 21 to 27 and 45, Figures 24 to 27, the mounting topics and the Junos CLI listing of the chassis hardware. Juniper's own straight-on studio photographs ex4100-f-48t-front-high.jpg and ex4100-f-48t-rear-high.jpg (1500 px wide JPEGs from the maker's public image library, no terms of use stated on the files), which supply every position below. The HPE PSNow datasheet (a00150781enw) was tried once and did not answer, so no datasheet figure is used. Nothing of the guide or the photographs is copied here: every face is drawn new from measurements. No Visio stencil, 3D model or other held photograph of the EX4100-F was available, so none was used. End of life was searched 2026-10-22: no Juniper notice for the EX4100-F was found (a reseller tracker lists the EX4100 family as supported with no dates), so the lifecycle is none announced.

status-block.note: Figures 26 and 28 and Tables 22 and 25 - a dark plate at the right end holds the chassis lamps SYS, ALM, MST and CLD (left column) and the port mode lamps SPD, DX and EN (right column, three rows: the PoE lamp is not available on a model without PoE, Table 25 note, and the photograph prints no PoE legend), each lamp above its legend, a round blue Factory Reset/Mode button with a list icon and the USB Type-C console (CON). The columns centre at 425.9 and 431.6 mm. The lamps are very faint in the photograph and are placed from their legends.
